subject: HeliosPay launch: phased warm-up and temporary rate increase request
messages:
From: Paul Yang <paul.yang@heliospay.com>
To: Rachel Kim <rachel_kim@redwood.ai>
Cc: contracts@heliospay.com
Date: Sun, 15 Feb 2026 09:12:00 -0800
Subject: HeliosPay launch week traffic profile and warm-up

Hi Rachel —

Quick context: HeliosPay is going live with payments ML features next month. We expect a staggered rollout across three regions; first batch is US production pilot on March 3. Early estimate: 12k user requests/day the first week, ramping to ~120k/day by week 4. Peak QPS expected ~65 for short bursts (2–5 mins) during morning settlement windows.

We need a temporary quota bump and a warm-up plan so we don't hit 429s during the pilot. Can Redwood provision a phased increase over the first 7 days with canary routing to a fallback smaller model if needed? Attached is our traffic ramp spreadsheet and the draft SOW.

Key asks: 
- Temporary rate limits for 3/3–3/10 (target sustained QPS 20, burst 80)
- Canary window: 30 minutes after each new cohort flip with elevated logging hooks
- Contact for on-call during launch: (we'll provide a dedicated Slack channel)

Thanks — happy to jump on a quick call if helpful.

Paul Yang
Head of Integrations, HeliosPay
paul.yang@heliospay.com

Attachments: heliospay_traffic_ramp.xlsx, heliospay_SOW_draft.pdf

From: Rachel Kim <rachel_kim@redwood.ai>
To: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.ai>, Irene Choi <irene_choi@redwood.ai>, Marcus Lin <marcus_lin@redwood.ai>, Priyom Das <priyom_das@redwood.ai>
Cc: Paul Yang <paul.yang@heliospay.com>
Date: Sun, 15 Feb 2026 11:03:00 -0800
Subject: Re: HeliosPay launch week traffic profile and warm-up

Team — looping you in. HeliosPay asked for a temporary uplift and a short canary policy. I attached their workbook. Quick summary of our ask from sales/CS: 7-day phased uplift for the US pilot, target sustained QPS 20 with bursts to 80, canary windows, elevated logs, and an on-call path.

Irene: can you confirm product constraints (max sustained per-tenant qps, recommended model fallback, cache warm-up guidance)?
Marcus: can infra/ops create the quota ticket and map to the right GPU pool for a burst profile?
Karthik/Priyom: we're negotiating the SOW and need to lock the launch date and acceptance criteria in the next 48 hours.

If we can get a rough yes/no today, I'll finalize the warm-up cadence with HeliosPay.

Thanks,
Rachel Kim
Account Executive, Redwood Inference
rachel_kim@redwood.ai

From: Irene Choi <irene_choi@redwood.ai>
To: Rachel Kim <rachel_kim@redwood.ai>, Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.ai>, Marcus Lin <marcus_lin@redwood.ai>, Priyom Das <priyom_das@redwood.ai>
Date: Mon, 16 Feb 2026 08:15:00 -0800
Subject: Re: HeliosPay launch week traffic profile and warm-up

Thanks for the details — I reviewed the workbook. TL;DR: feasible with a few guardrails.

Constraints & recommendations:
- Per-tenant sustained QPS (recommended): 25 QPS on m-medium model family; sustained above that requires dedicated pool or lower-latency SKU.
- Bursts: we can support bursts to 80 QPS for short windows if we place them on the burst pool and enable pre-warm (30–60m) with prefix cache priming.
- Canary strategy: 5–10% traffic routed to canary variant for the first 30 minutes after each cohort flip. Add a rollback trigger if 5xxs >1% or median latency > 600ms for 5 consecutive minutes.
- Fallback model: use gpt-lite-10b as fallback for heavy tails; it reduces per-token cost ~35% and latency by ~20% in our perf tests.

Operational asks from product/infra side (what we need from Sales/CS):
- Exact cohort activation timestamps (timezone-aware) and expected request distribution across the day (attached sheet has daily totals but we need per-hour slices for the first 72h).
- Signed temporary consumption exhibit (dates + quotas) so Ops can authorize a short-term quota policy.
- Slack channel + on-call escalation matrix.

I can commit to the configuration above once we have the hourly ramp and the temporary exhibit. Marcus, can you confirm whether we can assign the burst pool and create the quota ACL for HLSP-2026-01?

Irene Choi
Product Manager, Serving Runtime
irene_choi@redwood.ai

Acknowledged — we can do this. Plan and next steps: 

1) Quota ticket: I'll open SUP-1824 and request a temporary policy: Mar 3 00:00 PDT -> Mar 10 23:59 PDT, sustained 25 QPS, burst 80 QPS, canary slices (5–10%). Link below.
2) Pool assignment: reserve 2x burst nodes (n1-burst-8) for the US pilot window and enable pre-warm starting Mar 2 18:00 PDT.
3) Monitoring & alerts: ops will enable elevated traces for the canary and add alerts per Irene's rollback thresholds. Ops on-call is cc'd.
4) Ops handoff doc: Rachel/Priyom please add the hourly ramp slices into the sheet and add the signed temporary exhibit (consumption dates + limit). I'll only push the quota once the exhibit is uploaded and approved by Finance.

I'll create the ticket and post the runbook in the SUP ticket & the drive folder.

Marcus Lin
Infrastructure Lead, Redwood Inference
marcus_lin@redwood.ai
